newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-DORTMUND HOPE FOR INSPIRATION FROM EURO 96.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DORTMUND HOPE FOR INSPIRATION FROM EURO 96.

text.p: Borussia Dortmund are
hoping memories of Germany's Euro 96 successes in Manchester
will help them reach their first European Cup final.
The German champions take a goal advantage into the second
leg of their semifinal against Manchester United in two weeks'
time after Wednesday's home leg.
Dortmund know they will face an intense atmosphere at Old
Trafford, but internationals like libero Matthias Sammer and
midfielder Andy Moeller have fond memories of the ground where
Germany played four of six European championship games.
"An important point in our favour is that we know the
surroundings," Moeller said. "We have many players who played
there at the European championships.
"Manchester are a strong side at home. We are going there
knowing we haven't made it yet because you can't relax with a
1-0 lead."
Germany played some close games at Old Trafford last June,
including a tense 0-0 draw with Italy and a tight quarter-final
against Croatia.
Dortmund defender Juergen Kohler has bad memories of Old
Trafford after an injury in the opening game forced him out of
the rest of the tournament. But Sammer scored two crucial goals
at the ground against Russia and Croatia and Moeller struck a
spectacular effort in the first match against the Czech
Republic.
Dortmund was forced to field a second choice side for the
first leg because of a suspension to Sammer and injuries to
Kohler and strikers Karlheinz Riedle and Stephane Chapuisat.
But all four are expected to play at Old Trafford.
Manchester United will feel unlucky not to have managed a
draw on Wednesday. Alex Ferguson's side went close several times
and only the post stopped Nicky Butt from scoring in the second
half.
"They had a bit of luck tonight. Maybe it will be our turn
next time," Ferguson said. "The marvellous atmosphere at Old
Trafford will help us and the players will play better, I can
assure you of that."
United will be without influential midfielder Roy Keane who
was shown his second yellow card of the competition for what
seemed to be a fair challenge on Dortmund's Portuguese
midfielder Paulo Sousa. "I thought Roy was very unlucky. I know
I have defended him a lot of times but that was really
ridiculous tonight." Ferguson added.
